title: Stallioneer Inventory, Control, and Options unification checkpoint
content:
Stallioneer had a consolidation pass focused on making the app feel less like separate experiments and more like one consistent library workspace. The trajectory is clearer now: Inventory is the daily working page, Control owns library vocabulary, Options owns appearance/export/destructive maintenance, and Auth remains the account and permission source.

What changed:

  • Bulk was retired: the standalone Bulk page was removed during development, with a code comment left behind for history. Its useful selection workflows now live inside Inventory.
  • Inventory became the center: selected-book controls, live tag filtering, AND/OR tag mode, ctrl-click tag selection, and selected collection/status/location actions are now available without leaving the main catalog.
  • Control was split out: tags, collections, and locations moved into a dedicated Control page so vocabulary editing is separate from export/settings work.
  • Options got narrower and safer: the page now focuses on theme selection, CSV/PDF export, and a guarded delete-library flow that requires the visible book count before removal.
  • The Perihelion style became the model: Control and Options now use the same top-left page title, tab row, active panels, and theme-card language that has been working well on Perihelion.

This worked because the app stopped protecting old page boundaries. Bulk had been useful for prototyping, but folding its best behavior into Inventory makes Stallioneer simpler to use now and easier to port later to Android and Windows 98-style surfaces.
